feature: The Sections row: choosing which parts of the panel you get
summary: The right hand panel now has a Sections row at its foot that opens a list of the sections you are allowed to say no to, and the panel has been photographed and measured for the first time. Turning Motion off saves 81 points of panel, which is a real number and a smaller one than the feature's own claim implies.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. Flags are on by default. Window 1280x900, which gives the panel a scrolling area 841 points tall.

try.do: Draw a rectangle and click it with the Select tool.
Read the row at the very foot of the panel. It says "Sections · 5 hidden" before you have hidden anything.
Click that row to open the list.
Click the Sections row again to close the list, and look at how much shorter the panel got.
Open the list again and press Use Automatic For All. Motion comes back.
Type some text, click it, and see the panel grow past the bottom of the window.

evaluate: Turning Motion off saves 81 points out of a panel that is 552 points tall for a plain box in an 841 point space. It was not scrolling before and it is not scrolling now. Is 81 points worth a control at the foot of the panel?

With a piece of text picked the panel is 1046 points in an 841 point space, and with Motion off it is 965. Still scrolling. Is the feature aimed at the wrong thing, given that the sections that actually cost room are Effects and Layout rather than Motion?

The row says "5 hidden" in a brand new document where you have hidden nothing. Those five are sections the automatic rule left out because the document has no measurement, no component and no layout yet. Should the count only ever mean sections YOU turned off?

The list says the difference in words under each name ("Automatic, not needed in this document yet" against "Always hidden"), but the row's count does not. Is the word in the list enough, or does the count have to agree with it?
Does the foot of the panel feel like the right home for this, or would you look for it in a menu?
rough: The Mac's screen has been locked since 2026-09-15 08:44, so a walk refuses to run. These five pictures ARE real captures of the window, taken by forcing the run with PHOTONZ_ALLOW_LOCKED_WALK=1 after confirming the camera still works on a locked Mac. The picture is real; the walk is not an official pass.

The count on the row is wrong in spirit: "5 hidden" the moment you open a new document, when the whole point of printing a count was to be the one cue that something is missing. A cue that is always on says nothing. Written up as its own question above rather than changed, because which of the two meanings it should carry is a call for the user, not for the loop.

The switches in the list did not line up: Motion's and Arrange's sat half way across the row because their one line of small print made the switch shrink to fit, while everybody else's sat at the right edge. Fixed in this task, and the second picture is the fixed version.

The walk written for this feature had never run, and two things in it were wrong. It committed a piece of text with Escape, which throws the text away, so the stage that was meant to prove a Text section arrives proved nothing. And it closed the Sections list with Escape, which in a scripted run reaches the canvas and clears the selection while the list stays open. Both fixed.

Whether Escape closes this list for a person at the keyboard is still unknown. A walk posts keys at the editor window and this list lives in a window of its own, so the walk cannot tell. Filed as a question to look into rather than as a bug.
